primaryText: You may have tea or coffee.

readings.name: implies: you may have coffee and you may have tea

comment: Kamp's deontic free choice, the original observation.

primaryText: It might be here or there.

readings.name: implies: it might be here and it might be there

comment: Epistemic free choice.

primaryText: Either there isn't a bathroom in this house, or it's in a funny place.

readings.name: existential: either no bathroom, or a bathroom in a funny place

comment: The bathroom disjunction: the negation of the first disjunct entails a witness for the pronoun in the second.

primaryText: Ethan has a husband. He's standing outside.
context: It is known that if Ethan is married, he is married to a man.
comment: The indefinite introduces a discourse referent for the pronoun.

primaryText: Ethan is married. He's standing outside.
context: It is known that if Ethan is married, he is married to a man.
comment: Contextually equivalent to (10a) but without a linguistic antecedent: the formal link condition.

primaryText: Either John has no husband, or he's standing outside.
comment: Anaphora across a disjunction with an indefinite in the negated first disjunct.

primaryText: Either John isn't married, or he's standing outside.
comment: The formal link condition holds across disjunctions too.

primaryText: Either Sue didn't buy a sage plant, or she bought eight others along with it.
comment: The pronoun does not project uniqueness in a bathroom disjunction, against an E-type analysis; adapted from Heim's sage plant sentence.

primaryText: Either John doesn't own a shirt, or it's in the wardrobe.

alternatives.form: John owns a shirt, and it's in the wardrobe.

comment: The conditional-uniqueness oddness is shared by the conjunctive discourse (16b), so it is not special to disjunction.

primaryText: Either Gennaro doesn't have a credit card, or he paid with it.
context: Wondering how Gennaro paid for dinner.

readings.name: existential: consistent with a credit card he did not pay with
universal: every credit card was used to pay

comment: Universal truth conditions for bathroom disjunctions are too strong.

primaryText: It's possible that either there's no bathroom in this house or it's in a surprising place.

readings.name: entails: it's possible that there's no bathroom in this house
entails: it's possible that there's a bathroom in this house in a surprising place

comment: Free choice with anaphora under an epistemic modal: the second inference combines material from both disjuncts.

primaryText: You may include no appendix, or keep it to a single page.

readings.name: entails: you may include no appendix
entails: you may include an appendix kept to a single page
entails: you may keep it to a single page

comment: Free choice with anaphora under a deontic modal; the classical schema's conclusion (25) has a free pronoun and is not the attested inference.

primaryText: Gabor didn't write a paper about free choice, but it was interesting.
comment: An indefinite under negation licenses no subsequent pronoun: the negative update of an existential introduces no anaphoric information.

primaryText: It's not true that Sue didn't buy a sage plant — she bought eight others along with it!
comment: A doubly negated indefinite licenses anaphora without a uniqueness inference: Double Negation Elimination holds for anaphoric information.

primaryText: No, Kafuku doesn't own no car — he drives it every day.
context: Answering: Does Kafuku own no car?
comment: A doubly negated existential introduces the same anaphoric information as its positive counterpart, which standard dynamic semantics cannot deliver.

primaryText: Either it's upstairs, or there is no bathroom.
comment: A backwards bathroom disjunction, cataphora that the asymmetric dynamic entries do not capture.

primaryText: Either Gennaro doesn't have a credit card, or he paid with it.
context: Gennaro has a credit card that he paid with and another that he did not.

readings.name: true in the context

comment: The derived truth conditions (70) are existential: true as soon as some credit card was used.

primaryText: Maybe there isn't a bathroom.
comment: The positive update passes when some possibility has no bathroom; the negative update passes when the state subsists in the positive update of the existential, that is, every possibility has a bathroom.

primaryText: There might be a bathroom and it might be upstairs.
comment: Modal subordination: the externally static test semantics for modals does not license this anaphora.

primaryText: There might be coffee or tea.

readings.name: entails: there might be coffee and there might be tea

comment: Free choice without anaphora: modal disjunction requires both disjuncts to be possible.

primaryText: It's impossible that there's coffee or tea.

readings.name: entails: no coffee is possible and no tea is possible

comment: Dual prohibition is preserved because the negative update of modal disjunction is untouched.

primaryText: Either it's possible there's no bathroom, or it's possible it's upstairs.

readings.name: entails: it's possible there's no bathroom, and it's possible there's a bathroom upstairs

comment: Wide free choice with anaphora, beyond the externally static modals of the analysis.

primaryText: Every student read The Master and Margarita or The White Guard.

readings.name: entails: some student read The Master and Margarita
entails: some student read The White Guard

comment: The distributive inference of a disjunction under a universal.

primaryText: Every student either didn't read a novel, or wrote a report on it.

readings.name: entails: some student didn't read a novel
entails: some student read a novel and wrote a report on it

comment: The distributive inference with anaphora, with the universal as the dual of the existential and disjunction as modal disjunction.

primaryText: Not every linguist is attending the plenary talk. She's smoking outside.
discourseSegments: Not every linguist is attending the plenary talk.
comment: The dual treatment of the universal wrongly predicts that a negated universal introduces a singular discourse referent; a plural setting is needed.

primaryText: If either there's no bathroom or it's upstairs, this house needs to be renovated.

readings.name: entails: if there's no bathroom, this house needs to be renovated
entails: if there's a bathroom upstairs, this house needs to be renovated

comment: Simplification of disjunctive antecedents with anaphora, left for future work.

primaryText: It's not required that you include an appendix and keep it to a single page.

readings.name: negative free choice with anaphora

comment: Negative free choice with an anaphoric dependency inside the conjunction, derived by a precondition on the negative update of conjunction.
